profile.description: GCP c4a-highcpu-32 / Axion Neoverse-V2, Nemotron 3.5 streaming 0.6B, int8, cache-aware streaming over WebSocket. Three workers of 8 threads over a 24-cpu slice, the remaining 8 cpus reserved for whatever generates the load. C=16 is QUALIFIED as of 2026-09-22: two independent 1800 s soaks on fresh fleets with different seeds, 7738 utterances and 56488 audio-seconds, zero established streams lost, zero stalls over 125948 published deltas, and every transcript byte-identical to the unloaded reference. It is a floor, not a ceiling: one stream costs 15.85 ms of compute per 320 ms of audio, so C=16 asks this fleet for about a quarter of itself. The knee above it is not yet measured -- the 2026-09-22 C=24 and C=32 rungs were invalid, having been run against a fleet that could only connect 24 streams.

hardware.smt_policy: OFF; one thread per physical core
hardware.notes: bf16/sve/sve2 are present and the binary issues none of them. That is three unspent levers, not a defect, and --dispatch-map prints them as IDLE so the gap stays visible.

build.notes: No OpenBLAS on this host, so gemm.f32 resolves to our own sgemm. That is what a clean clone gets here.

notes: 3x8 replaced 1x24 on 2026-09-20 and the reason is measured, not stylistic. At an equal 24-cpu budget the useful audio per cpu reads 1x12 0.806, 1x24 0.537, 2x12 0.800, 3x8 0.826: two independent 12-thread domains deliver twice one of them, so the domains do not contend, while one 24-thread domain loses a third of its per-cpu throughput inside the step. The limit is intra-step thread scaling past about 12 threads, not cross-worker interference.

The 1x24 ceiling of 16 recorded in this file before 2026-09-20 was taken while the scheduler could freeze for tens of seconds on a blocking peek (serving-findings F15). Every topology number from before that fix is retired, not merely superseded.

http_threads is NOT the compute width. It is the server's HTTP thread pool and a WebSocket stream holds one for its whole life, so it is the fleet's connection ceiling; the compute pool sizes itself from each worker's affinity mask, which prefork_threads sets. 96 is 3 workers x 32 and leaves headroom above the 64 streams the ladder reached.

batch_window_ms is 0 because widening the ready set did not move the ceiling: 40 ms took the mean ready set from 3.69 to 5.85 at c=16 and the ceiling stayed at 16, and 80 ms took it to 7.98 and cost a rung. Kept at 0 until something makes the fixed cost matter again.

MYNAH_ASR_THREADS.why: must be ABSENT: each worker's pool sizes itself from sched_getaffinity, which is what makes prefork_threads and server_cpus mean anything. Setting it silently overrides every worker's slice at once.

MYNAH_ASR_CAPS.why: must be ABSENT: the runtime probe must choose the kernel, and dispatch_required is what checks it chose right.

OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS.why: must be ABSENT: no OpenBLAS is linked here, and a variable that does nothing is a variable someone will later believe did something.

MYNAH_ASR_POOL_SPIN_US.why: must be ABSENT: the default spin has never been swept on this box. The sibling engine found a 16x longer spin budget on aarch64 worth measurable p95; that sweep is owed here and this line is the record that it has not been done.

MYNAH_ASR_STACK_SOLO.why: the binary's DEFAULT, so it must NOT be exported -- it is recorded here because it is load-bearing, not because a deployment should set it. A ready set of one goes through the stacked encoder path. Measured on this box, one binary, flag as the only difference, arms alternated, c=8 on a fresh server each time -- ON 105/104/103 ms emission lag p95, OFF 175/175 ms. The step itself goes 86.7 -> 16.8 ms for a lone stream. It matters most at low concurrency, which on a 3x8 fleet is every worker's common case.

gates.notes: 320 ms is not a taste: it is (lookahead + 1) x 80 ms, the cadence the model itself sets, so a stream whose emission lag exceeds it is falling behind the audio. ttfp_p95_ms is null because this repo cannot yet defend a number for it, NOT because TTFP does not matter. It has a load-independent floor of about 1545 ms on this build and corpus -- 1544 at C=8, 1545 at C=16, 1646 at C=32 -- plus a queueing term that appears only past the knee (1925 at C=40, 2827 at C=64). The earlier note here claimed the floor was leading silence; that holds for samples/en/fleurs_long.wav, which is silent until 23.2 s, and NOT for the three clips actually used, whose onsets are 0.02, 0.18 and 0.64 s. Roughly one second is unaccounted for. A TTFP gate needs that second explained and a corpus trimmed to speech onset, in that order.

measured_short_run_safe.what_this_licenses: Comparisons against other 90 s runs on this box. Nothing else. It is the point the ladder selected for qualification, not a supported capacity.

long_soak_qualified.what_this_licenses: A promise of this concurrency on this box shape, this model, this quant and this topology, for streams of this corpus's shape. It licenses nothing about a machine of a different size: the per-stream cost is a function of how many cores walk the weights.
long_soak_qualified.speech_to_first_partial_verdict: BAD against the UX guardrail (>1800 ms p95), REPORTED and not a serving gate. The paired load penalty is +86 ms p95, so the fleet contributes 4% of that wait; the rest belongs to the checkpoint's emission delay and to this corpus, whose long class runs to 42 s. On the 27 committed clips the same build read 1251 ms p95. It is a real product figure and it is not a server defect.

model_quality_reported.note: NOT a serving gate. A word this checkpoint gets wrong unloaded is not a defect of the fleet; serving correctness is the byte-identical parity against the unloaded reference, which passed on all 498 clips.

measured.overload_behaviour: Graceful. Zero lost established streams and zero admission rejections at EVERY rung through C = 64: above the knee this fleet degrades by getting slow, never by dropping work that was already accepted. Do not read C = 64 as supported -- losing no streams is the floor the engine owes, not a capacity claim, and at C = 64 the backlog is seven times the gate.

saturation.note: Two duties, because one cannot express this. The BATCHED step plateaus at 0.790/0.810/0.815 across C = 32/36/40 while concurrency, backlog and mean batch all keep rising -- that part is real. But total model execution is 0.896/0.928/0.940: the finalization tail is the model too, and the three-way split used to charge it to runnable_idle. Subtracting finalize from runnable_idle leaves 0.029/0.014/0.012, and THAT is the avoidable idle. There is no 13-14 % of reclaimable wall on this box; at C = 40 the fleet runs the model 94 % of the time. The serving question is efficiency, not utilisation.

finalize_composition.note: Teardown -- done frame, session close, bookkeeping, reset -- costs nothing measurable, and so does sched_feed_tail: mynah_asr_stream_finish is 99.8 % of the whole finalize phase, recomputed from the raw per-worker dumps. It runs at B = 1, one slot at a time in scheduler phase 5, and the per-call cost is FLAT at ~82 ms across all three loads while the mean batch of ordinary steps goes 2.11 -> 3.12 -> 4.71. A fixed cost per UTTERANCE that does not amortise with load because it is not batched. Removing it entirely returns at most 12.5 % of wall at C = 40, against the +25 % of offered load that C = 32 -> C = 40 asks for, so batching it is PREDICTED not to be sufficient on its own.

cost_model_on_the_serving_path.note: Fitted from mynah_asr_step_b_wall_ms_sum / mynah_asr_step_b_count on the 1x24 topology, i.e. the step AS THE SCHEDULER CALLS IT. The bench in isolation says b = 4.58. These constants have NOT been refitted for 3x8 and must not be applied to it: b is a function of how many cores walk the weights, and 8 threads per worker is a different function from 24.

solo_group_ab.note: The third OFF rung is the pre-F15 stall, not a property of the arm. It landing in the CONTROL arm is what rules the change out as its cause -- a ladder run just before this A/B had shown the failure twice with the change ON, which on its own would have been read as a regression.

measured.ladder_note: finalize_share is null on nine rungs ON PURPOSE. The campaign harness printed that column against a denominator about 3x too small, and the raw per-worker dumps that would correct it were overwritten by a later run on every rung but C = 32/36/40. A wrong number removed beats a wrong number kept; see docs/serving-findings.md F21. Every other column recomputes from the raw dumps to within 0.003.

history.why_not_promoted: Every serving gate passes and no stream was lost in ten minutes. It does not qualify for two reasons. Transcripts were not checked -- 0 utterances scored against a reference, because no manifest exists in this repo and make fetch-stress-bank has never been run -- and the profile's own condition is zero losses AND transcripts checked. And TTFP p95 is 1657 ms against a 1160 ms limit; that is load-independent (1544 ms at C=8) so it is not a capacity signal, but the explanation this file used to give for it -- leading silence -- is wrong for this corpus, whose clips start speaking at 0.02, 0.18 and 0.64 s. About a second of pipeline latency is unexplained. The limit is not being moved.

history.what_this_licenses: A promise of this concurrency on this box shape, this model, this quant and this topology, for streams of this corpus's shape. It licenses nothing about a machine of a different size: the per-stream cost is a function of how many cores walk the weights.

what_each_means.qualified_safe_concurrency: survived two independent 1800 s soaks on fresh fleets with different seeds, every registered bound. This is the only number that may be promised.
what_each_means.short_run_last_good_concurrency: highest 180 s SCREEN that cleared every bound, at 0.973 model duty. A screen disqualifies; it never promotes. Not promised.
what_each_means.first_failed_concurrency: lowest screen where bounds broke -- finalization 619 ms, backlog 0.744 s and per-window drift together, not one threshold by a margin.
what_each_means.headroom_to_first_failure: (104 - 80) / 80. Chosen over C=88, which clears the screen but sits 18% below first failure at 0.921 duty, because a production point should survive a bad day.

measured_cores_used.note: cumulative cpu-seconds per worker, differenced over the run. NOT workers x model_duty x threads, which reads 26.3 here and overstates by about 20% because model_duty is the scheduler thread's fraction and says nothing about the pool's occupancy during it. Why the remaining ~8 core-equivalents go unused at saturation is NOT established.

provenance.measured_on: gabrielemastrapasqua@c4a-highcpu-32, Linux 7.0.0-1011-gcp, loadavg < 0.5 at start, one fresh server per rung
provenance.commit: a941390 (capacity ladder C = 8..64), 0761a35 (finalize composition at C = 32/36/40)
provenance.harness: tools/bench/stream_load.py --mode soak --streams C --duration 90 --warmup 10 --window 30 --bank short,medium --lookahead 3, generator pinned to cpus 24-31, one process per stream, 25 s warm-up run discarded before each measured rung
provenance.corpus: samples/en/fleurs_1521.wav (7.4 s), samples/en/fleurs_1534.wav (11.9 s), tests/audio/test_en.wav (4.3 s); mean utterance about 6.8 audio-s
notes: The capacity stated is for the 24-cpu SLICE, not for the 32-cpu box, and it is not scaled up. The load generator is one process per stream and shares the machine; the 8 reserved cpus are what keeps it out of the measurement.

status stays `screened` and long_soak_qualified stays null until an independent soak of at least 10 minutes holds C = 32 with zero lost streams and transcripts checked. Rungs here are 90 s, and serving-findings F12 exists because a short ladder once promoted a topology that lost streams over ten minutes.

Finalize is a per-utterance cost, so this curve is a function of the corpus's mean utterance length as well as of the machine. A deployment whose utterances are much shorter than 6.8 s should expect the knee to the LEFT of 36.

CLOSED since the previous revision of this file: the stall in which every stream received a first partial and then nothing for tens of seconds. Root cause and fix in serving-findings F15/F17 -- a blocking recv(MSG_PEEK) on a socket with two readers. It was never a prefork property; prefork only made it likelier.

The 2026-09-20 revision of this file carried a finalize share about 3x too large and a duty that excluded the finalization tail from model execution. Both were found by recomputing the campaign's own table from the raw dumps rather than by re-running it, and both are recorded in docs/serving-findings.md F21 rather than quietly edited away.
